title: Ye Announces a Trio of New U.S. Stadium Shows
summary: West returns to Chicago for a pair of homecoming shows on Sept. 3 and 4.
contentText:
Ye (formerly Kanye West ) has been performing one-off shows all over the globe throughout 2026, and he’s added three more stadium dates in the U.S. before year’s end.

West will be celebrating spooky season with a Halloween show slated for Houston’s NRG Stadium on Oct. 31, before heading to Jerry’s World for a concert at the massive AT&T Stadium in Dallas on Nov. 7. The 49-year-old also has a show lined up in Phoenix, where he’ll take over State Farm Stadium on Nov. 21.

Ye will return home this week, Thursday (Sept. 3) and Friday (Sept. 4), for a pair of shows in Chicago at Soldier Field. In October, West will travel to Indonesia for a show on Oct. 24.

West hasn’t announced a full-length tour, but has been performing spot dates across the globe throughout 2026. He returned to Mexico for the first time in nearly two decades, when he performed two shows in Mexico City in January to kick off the year.

On the heels of Bully ‘s arrival in March, Ye performed a pair of shows at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles. The April 1 and 3 dates grossed $32.6 million across 149,000 tickets sold, per Billboard Boxscore.

However, backlash remained and other entities weren’t as willing to forgive Ye for his controversies and repeated hate speech and antisemitic remarks since 2022, which axed lucrative deals West had with adidas, Universal Music Group, Gap and Balenciaga. Ye’s summer headlining gig at Wireless Fest in London was canceled after the U.K. denied him a visa to travel to the country. He also had a France show postponed and concerts in Italy, Russia and Poland canceled this year.

The 49-year-old has been able to book select dates in the U.S., which have included shows in Tampa Bay, San Antonio and New Orleans in 2026. Around the world, Ye’s performed in Kazakhstan, Georgia, Albania, Spain, Turkey and the Netherlands over the course of the year.

West released his Bully album through Gamma in March, which debuted at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 with 152,000 total album-equivalent units.
